title: Why does copying mp4 subtitles into MKV fail?
fullTitle: FFmpeg -c copy of mov_text to MKV Writes 0 of 3 Streams; -c:s srt Works

scenes.narration: You copy an mp4 into an m k v with dash c copy, and its subtitles are mov text. Does it fail, or change? We build a five second synthetic clip with three cues, copy it every way we can, and read the stream list.
captions: Copy mov_text subtitles into MKV: fail, or change?
We read the stream list and the cues, two ways.

scenes.narration: The source has video, a tone, and three cues, one in italics, as mov text. Controls: copied into a dot mov, it stays mov text; a subrip m k v stays subrip. Readers: f f probe, and the raw bytes in Node.
captions: Controls: mov_text into .mov, subrip into .mkv: unchanged.
Readers: ffprobe; raw bytes (codec id, cue text).

scenes.narration: Now the question. Dash c copy into dot m k v: f f m peg stops, says the subtitle codec is not supported, and leaves a two hundred ninety three byte stub. Zero of three streams. Both readers find no cue text.
captions: -c copy to .mkv: 0 of 3 streams, a 293 byte stub.
ffprobe and the raw bytes: no streams, no cue text.

scenes.narration: Name the codec. Dash c colon s, s r t, or dash c colon s, a s s: video and audio still copied, three cues, the same times to the millisecond, italics kept. Leave the subtitle out instead, and you get two streams, no text.
captions: -c:s srt and -c:s ass: 3 streams, 3 cues, same times.

scenes.narration: Give no codec options at all, and nothing fails. The subtitle becomes a s s, the audio is converted to vorbis, and the cues land three milliseconds late. Text survives, but you did not copy what you thought.
captions: No options: ass subtitle, vorbis audio, cues +3 ms.
The stream list shows it; the exit status does not.

scenes.narration: The other way is just as strict. Subrip into an mp4 with dash c copy fails and writes zero bytes. Dash c colon s, mov text, works: three cues, same times, italics. Mov text stores six packets for three cues; matroska stores three.
captions: subrip -> .mp4 with -c copy: 0 bytes. -c:s mov_text: works.
mov_text: 6 packets for 3 cues. subrip, ass: 3.

scenes.narration: Name the subtitle codec for the container: srt or a s s for m k v, mov text for mp4. Then read the stream list. Not tested: other subtitle formats, picture subtitles, players, and builds other than six point one.
captions: srt or ass for MKV, mov_text for MP4. Then run ffprobe.
Not tested: image subtitles, players, other builds.
